note: CSB text checked verbatim against BibleGateway (CSB): the first 30 on Oct 15, 2026; the rest on Oct 20, 2026 (each entry's 'verified'). Copied from the page with a script and checked byte for byte (SHA-256) against the page, so scheduled runs never need the browser. Poetry line breaks are shown as ' / '. A speech quote mark the verse doesn't open and close itself is dropped. Quote verbatim; mark partial verses with an ellipsis. Read the context and the note before use; notes flag cautions (no prosperity readings, sentence fragments). 'stories' holds verified narrative passages for Get Back Up carousels. Mark each use in 'used' and log it in SOURCES.md.

verses.text: Therefore, submit to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
Haven’t I commanded you: be strong and courageous? Do not be afraid or discouraged, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.
verses.note: God's command to Joshua as he takes over from Moses; a closing speech quote mark in the source is dropped.

verses.text: God—he clothes me with strength / and makes my way perfect.
He trains my hands for war; / my arms can bend a bow of bronze.
verses.note: War imagery: keep the fight spiritual, never literal violence.

verses.text: The LORD is my light and my salvation— / whom should I fear? / The LORD is the stronghold of my life— / whom should I dread?
A person’s steps are established by the LORD, / and he takes pleasure in his way. / Though he falls, he will not be overwhelmed, / because the LORD supports him with his hand.
God is our refuge and strength, / a helper who is always found / in times of trouble.
My flesh and my heart may fail, / but God is the strength of my heart, / my portion forever.
Blessed be the LORD, my rock / who trains my hands for battle / and my fingers for warfare.
verses.note: War imagery: keep the fight spiritual.

verses.text: Iron sharpens iron, / and one person sharpens another.
The wicked flee when no one is pursuing them, / but the righteous are as bold as a lion.
Do not fear, for I am with you; / do not be afraid, for I am your God. / I will strengthen you; I will help you; / I will hold on to you with my righteous right hand.

After I made an inspection, I stood up and said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, “Don’t be afraid of them. Remember the great and awe-inspiring Lord, and fight for your countrymen, your sons and daughters, your wives and homes.”
verses.note: Rebuilding the wall under threat. Apply to protecting the home spiritually; never imply violence.

verses.text: Mankind, he has told each of you what is good / and what it is the LORD requires of you: / to act justly, / to love faithfulness, / and to walk humbly with your God.
Be alert, stand firm in the faith, be courageous, be strong.
verses.note: Pair with v14 (do everything in love) in the caption when it fits.

verses.text: We are afflicted in every way but not crushed; we are perplexed but not in despair; we are persecuted but not abandoned; we are struck down but not destroyed.

But he said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is perfected in weakness.” Therefore, I will most gladly boast all the more about my weaknesses, so that Christ’s power may reside in me.
Let us not get tired of doing good, for we will reap at the proper time if we don’t give up.
Finally, be strengthened by the Lord and by his vast strength.
Put on the full armor of God so that you can stand against the schemes of the devil.
For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but one of power, love, and sound judgment.
Share in suffering as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.

Therefore, since we also have such a large cloud of witnesses surrounding us, let us lay aside every hindrance and the sin that so easily ensnares us. Let us run with endurance the race that lies before us,
verses.note: Sentence continues into v2: quote as partial with an ellipsis.

verses.text: No discipline seems enjoyable at the time, but painful. Later on, however, it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.
verses.note: Context is God's discipline of His children; fine for training and hardship, keep God as the one who trains.

verses.text: Blessed is the one who endures trials, because when he has stood the test he will receive the crown of life that God has promised to those who love him.
Be sober-minded, be alert. Your adversary the devil is prowling around like a roaring lion, looking for anyone he can devour.
The God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory in Christ, will himself restore, establish, strengthen, and support you after you have suffered a little while.
No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us.
You are from God, little children, and you have conquered them, because the one who is in you is greater than the one who is in the world.
Trust in the LORD with all your heart, / and do not rely on your own understanding; / in all your ways know him, / and he will make your paths straight.
Be strong and courageous; don’t be terrified or afraid of them. For the LORD your God is the one who will go with you; he will not leave you or abandon you.
verses.note: Moses to Israel before they cross into the land (repeated to Joshua in v. 8). The closing speech quote mark in the source is dropped.

verses.text: Even when I go through the darkest valley, / I fear no danger, / for you are with me; / your rod and your staff—they comfort me.
verses.note: Presence in the darkest valley, not exemption from it.

verses.text: The LORD is near the brokenhearted; / he saves those crushed in spirit.
He brought me up from a desolate pit, / out of the muddy clay, / and set my feet on a rock, / making my steps secure.
verses.note: David waiting on the LORD; rescue from the pit.

verses.text: The LORD is for me; I will not be afraid. / What can a mere mortal do to me?
Your word is a lamp for my feet / and a light on my path.
verses.note: The Hebrew letter heading (Nun) is not part of the verse.

verses.text: On the day I called, you answered me; / you increased strength within me.
He heals the brokenhearted / and bandages their wounds.
For his anger lasts only a moment, / but his favor, a lifetime. / Weeping may stay overnight, / but there is joy in the morning.
verses.note: David's thanksgiving after rescue. Not a promise that every hardship ends overnight.

verses.text: Commit your way to the LORD; / trust in him, and he will act,
verses.note: Ends with a comma; v. 6 continues. Quote as partial. Not a guarantee of outcomes.

verses.text: I lift my eyes toward the mountains. / Where will my help come from? / My help comes from the LORD, / the Maker of heaven and earth.
verses.note: Psalm 121:4 was used on Strike #2 (Oct 13); 121:1-2 is new.

verses.text: Cast your burden on the LORD, / and he will sustain you; / he will never allow the righteous to be shaken.
But you, LORD, are a shield around me, / my glory, and the one who lifts up my head.
verses.note: David fleeing Absalom.

verses.text: Guard your heart above all else, / for it is the source of life.
verses.note: Fits the breastplate (guarding the heart).

verses.text: The one who walks with the wise will become wise, / but a companion of fools will suffer harm.
A person’s heart plans his way, / but the LORD determines his steps.
A horse is prepared for the day of battle, / but victory comes from the LORD.
verses.note: Prepare, and know the victory is the LORD's. Not about real-world violence.

verses.text: A person who does not control his temper / is like a city whose wall is broken down.
verses.note: Self-control; pairs with anger posts.

verses.text: He gives strength to the faint / and strengthens the powerless.
verses.note: Isaiah 40:31 was used Oct 13.

verses.text: When you pass through the waters, / I will be with you, / and the rivers will not overwhelm you. / When you walk through the fire, / you will not be scorched, / and the flame will not burn you.
verses.note: Spoken to Israel; a promise of God's presence, never of immunity from hardship.

verses.text: Do not remember the past events; / pay no attention to things of old. / Look, I am about to do something new; / even now it is coming. Do you not see it? / Indeed, I will make a way in the wilderness, / rivers in the desert.
verses.note: To Israel about a new exodus; use as God's pattern of making a way, not a personal guarantee.

verses.text: For the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, has said: / “You will be delivered by returning and resting; / your strength will lie in quiet confidence. / But you are not willing.”
verses.note: A rebuke: Israel refused God's way of rest. If quoted, keep 'But you are not willing' or quote partial with ellipsis and don't strip the warning's meaning.

verses.text: How beautiful on the mountains / are the feet of the herald, / who proclaims peace, / who brings news of good things, / who proclaims salvation, / who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!”
verses.note: Behind the 'feet... readiness for the gospel of peace' (Eph 6:15) and Romans 10:15.

verses.text: Let’s examine and probe our ways, / and turn back to the LORD.
verses.note: The Hebrew letter heading (Nun) is not part of the verse.

verses.text: The LORD your God is among you, / a warrior who saves. / He will rejoice over you with gladness. / He will be quiet in his love. / He will delight in you with singing.
verses.note: Spoken to Zion. The closing quote mark in the source is dropped.

verses.text: Come, let’s return to the LORD. / For he has torn us, / and he will heal us; / he has wounded us, / and he will bind up our wounds.
verses.note: Israel's call to return; the next verses show the repentance was shallow (6:4). Use as an invitation, not cheap grace.

verses.text: Tear your hearts, / not just your clothes, / and return to the LORD your God. / For he is gracious and compassionate, / slow to anger, abounding in faithful love, / and he relents from sending disaster.
verses.note: Real repentance, not show.

verses.text: I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you; I will remove your heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
verses.note: God's promise to Israel of a new heart; fulfilled in the new covenant.

verses.text: And if someone overpowers one person, two can resist him. A cord of three strands is not easily broken.
verses.note: Ecclesiastes 4:10 was used Oct 13.

verses.text: You will certainly wear out both yourself and these people who are with you, because the task is too heavy for you. You can’t do it alone.
verses.note: Jethro to Moses: share the load. Opening quote mark in the source.

verses.text: Come to me, all of you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.
verses.note: Opening quote mark in the source; v. 29-30 continue Jesus's words.

verses.text: Stay awake and pray, so that you won’t enter into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.
verses.note: Jesus to the sleeping disciples in Gethsemane. Closing quote mark in the source is dropped.

verses.text: For what does it benefit someone to gain the whole world and yet lose his life?
Then he said to them all, “If anyone wants to follow after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross daily, and follow me.
verses.note: Daily surrender.

verses.text: No one has greater love than this: to lay down his life for his friends.
verses.note: Jesus's love for his friends; can frame sacrificial love at home. Never glorify violence.

verses.text: I have told you these things so that in me you may have peace. You will have suffering in this world. Be courageous! I have conquered the world.
verses.note: Closing quote mark in the source is dropped.

verses.text: And not only that, but we also boast in our afflictions, because we know that affliction produces endurance, endurance produces proven character, and proven character produces hope.
We know that all things work together for the good of those who love God, who are called according to his purpose.
verses.note: For those who love God, toward conformity to Christ (v. 29). Not a promise that bad things are good or that outcomes will be comfortable.

verses.text: Do not be conquered by evil, but conquer evil with good.
verses.note: The fight is spiritual; overcoming evil with good.

verses.text: Don’t you know that the runners in a stadium all race, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a way to win the prize.
verses.note: 1 Cor 9:27 was used Oct 15.

verses.text: Therefore, my dear brothers and sisters, be steadfast, immovable, always excelling in the Lord’s work, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.
verses.note: Grounded in the resurrection.

verses.text: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; the old has passed away, and see, the new has come!
and every proud thing that is raised up against the knowledge of God, and we take every thought captive to obey Christ.
verses.note: A sentence fragment (begins 'and'); v. 4 sets it up ('the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh'). Quote as partial with an ellipsis.

verses.text: I have been crucified with Christ, and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. The life I now live in the body, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.
Carry one another’s burdens; in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.
verses.note: Galatians 6:9 used on a Reel Oct 25.

verses.text: And be kind and compassionate to one another, forgiving one another, just as God also forgave you in Christ.
Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave himself for her
verses.note: No period; the sentence runs into v. 26. Quote with an ellipsis at the end. Read with 5:21 (mutual submission).

verses.text: I am able to do all things through him who strengthens me.
verses.note: About contentment in plenty and in need, not about winning anything you want. Never use it as a prosperity or success promise.

verses.text: Finally brothers and sisters, whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is just, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is commendable—if there is any moral excellence and if there is anything praiseworthy—dwell on these things.
verses.note: Guarding the mind.

verses.text: Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things.
Therefore encourage one another and build each other up as you are already doing.
For the training of the body has limited benefit, but godliness is beneficial in every way, since it holds promise for the present life and also for the life to come.
verses.note: Training the body matters some; godliness more.

verses.text: Fight the good fight of the faith. Take hold of eternal life to which you were called and about which you have made a good confession in the presence of many witnesses.
verses.note: Paul to Timothy; the fight is the fight of faith.

verses.text: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
verses.note: Paul near the end of his life.

verses.text: For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but one who has been tempted in every way as we are, yet without sin. Therefore, let us approach the throne of grace with boldness, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in time of need.

And let us consider one another in order to provoke love and good works, not neglecting to gather together, as some are in the habit of doing, but encouraging each other, and all the more as you see the day approaching.
verses.note: v. 24 ends with a comma; quote both together or mark partial.

verses.text: Consider it a great joy, my brothers and sisters, whenever you experience various trials, because you know that the testing of your faith produces endurance.
verses.note: v. 2 ends with a comma; quote both together.

verses.text: Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you.
verses.note: James 4:7 used on Strike #4 (Oct 15).

verses.text: Dear friends, I urge you as strangers and exiles to abstain from sinful desires that wage war against the soul.
verses.note: The war is inside: desires against the soul.

verses.text: casting all your cares on him, because he cares about you.
verses.note: Lowercase start; the sentence begins in v. 6 ('Humble yourselves... casting all your cares on him'). Quote with an ellipsis.

verses.text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
For this reason take up the full armor of God, so that you may be able to resist in the evil day, and having prepared everything, to take your stand.
verses.note: Armor Check: the call to take up the full armor.

verses.text: Stand, therefore, with truth like a belt around your waist, righteousness like armor on your chest,
verses.note: Armor Check: truth (belt, used Oct 18) and righteousness (breastplate). Ends with a comma; the sentence runs through v. 16. Quote partial with an ellipsis.

verses.text: and your feet sandaled with readiness for the gospel of peace.
verses.note: Armor Check: feet / readiness for the gospel of peace. Lowercase start; mark as partial.

verses.text: In every situation take up the shield of faith with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one.
verses.note: Armor Check: shield of faith.

verses.text: Take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit—which is the word of God.
verses.note: Armor Check: helmet of salvation and sword of the Spirit.

verses.text: Pray at all times in the Spirit with every prayer and request, and stay alert with all perseverance and intercession for all the saints.
verses.note: Armor Check: prayer and alertness.

verses.text: He made the one who did not know sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.
verses.note: Breastplate: the righteousness is Christ's, given to us.

verses.text: and be found in him, not having a righteousness of my own from the law, but one that is through faith in Christ—the righteousness from God based on faith.
verses.note: Breastplate: not a righteousness of my own. Lowercase start; mark as partial.

verses.text: And how can they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news.
verses.note: Feet: quotes Isaiah 52:7.

verses.text: Therefore, since we have been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.note: Feet / gospel of peace: peace with God.

verses.text: because everyone who has been born of God conquers the world. This is the victory that has conquered the world: our faith.
verses.note: Shield of faith. Lowercase start ('because'); mark as partial.

verses.text: For the word of God is living and effective and sharper than any double-edged sword, penetrating as far as the separation of soul and spirit, joints and marrow. It is able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
verses.note: Sword of the Spirit.

verses.text: But since we belong to the day, let us be self-controlled and put on the armor of faith and love, and a helmet of the hope of salvation.
verses.note: Helmet: the hope of salvation.

verses.text: He answered, “It is written: Man must not live on bread alone but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.”
verses.note: Sword: Jesus answers temptation with Scripture (quoting Deut 8:3).

verses.text: Jesus wept.
verses.note: Jesus wept at Lazarus's tomb before raising him. For posts about men grieving honestly.

verses.text: Then he said, “Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom.” And he said to him, “Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in paradise.”
verses.note: The criminal on the cross: never too late.

verses.text: I am sure of this, that he who started a good work in you will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus.
Restore the joy of your salvation to me, / and sustain me by giving me a willing spirit.
verses.note: Psalm 51:10 used on the David carousel (Oct 15).

stories.title: Moses: the man who ran
stories.note: He killed a man and fled for 40 years (Acts 7:23-30 gives the years; not verified here, so don't quote it). God sent him back anyway. Don't celebrate the killing; it's the fall.

verses.text: Years later, after Moses had grown up, he went out to his own people and observed their forced labor. He saw an Egyptian striking a Hebrew, one of his people.
Looking all around and seeing no one, he struck the Egyptian dead and hid him in the sand.
The next day he went out and saw two Hebrews fighting. He asked the one in the wrong, “Why are you attacking your neighbor?”
“Who made you a commander and judge over us?” the man replied. “Are you planning to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?” Then Moses became afraid and thought, “What I did is certainly known.”
When Pharaoh heard about this, he tried to kill Moses. But Moses fled from Pharaoh and went to live in the land of Midian, and sat down by a well.
therefore, go. I am sending you to Pharaoh so that you may lead my people, the Israelites, out of Egypt.”
But Moses asked God, “Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh and that I should bring the Israelites out of Egypt?”
He answered, “I will certainly be with you, and this will be the sign to you that I am the one who sent you: when you bring the people out of Egypt, you will all worship God at this mountain.”
But Moses replied to the LORD, “Please, Lord, I have never been eloquent—either in the past or recently or since you have been speaking to your servant—because my mouth and my tongue are sluggish.”
The LORD said to him, “Who placed a mouth on humans? Who makes a person mute or deaf, seeing or blind? Is it not I, the LORD?
Now go! I will help you speak and I will teach you what to say.”
By faith Moses, when he had grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter
and chose to suffer with the people of God rather than to enjoy the fleeting pleasure of sin.
For he considered reproach for the sake of Christ to be greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, since he was looking ahead to the reward.
By faith he left Egypt behind, not being afraid of the king’s anger, for Moses persevered as one who sees him who is invisible.

stories.title: Gideon: hiding in the winepress
stories.note: Called 'valiant warrior' while hiding. Victory is the LORD's (7:2). Keep battle language spiritual; no glorifying violence.

verses.text: The angel of the LORD came, and he sat under the oak that was in Ophrah, which belonged to Joash, the Abiezrite. His son Gideon was threshing wheat in the winepress in order to hide it from the Midianites.
Then the angel of the LORD appeared to him and said, “The LORD is with you, valiant warrior.”

Gideon said to him, “Please, my lord, if the LORD is with us, why has all this happened? And where are all his wonders that our ancestors told us about? They said, ‘Hasn’t the LORD brought us out of Egypt?’ But now the LORD has abandoned us and handed us over to Midian.”
The LORD turned to him and said, “Go in the strength you have and deliver Israel from the grasp of Midian. I am sending you!”
He said to him, “Please, Lord, how can I deliver Israel? Look, my family is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the youngest in my father’s family.”
“But I will be with you,” the LORD said to him. “You will strike Midian down as if it were one man.”
The LORD said to Gideon, “I will deliver you with the three hundred men who lapped and hand the Midianites over to you. But everyone else is to go home.”

stories.title: Jacob: wrestled, limped, renamed
stories.note: He walked away blessed and limping.

verses.text: Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him until daybreak.
When the man saw that he could not defeat him, he struck Jacob’s hip socket as they wrestled and dislocated his hip.
Then he said to Jacob, “Let me go, for it is daybreak.” But Jacob said, “I will not let you go unless you bless me.”
“What is your name?” the man asked. “Jacob,” he replied.
“Your name will no longer be Jacob,” he said. “It will be Israel because you have struggled with God and with men and have prevailed.”
Then Jacob asked him, “Please tell me your name.” But he answered, “Why do you ask my name?” And he blessed him there.
Jacob then named the place Peniel, “For I have seen God face to face,” he said, “yet my life has been spared.”
The sun shone on him as he passed by Penuel—limping because of his hip.

stories.title: Joseph: sold, jailed, faithful
stories.note: Gen 39:20 starts mid-sentence ('and had him thrown...'); mark partial. Joseph is a man wronged, not a man who fell: fits 'betrayed' and 'unfair' posts.

verses.text: When Midianite traders passed by, his brothers pulled Joseph out of the pit and sold him for twenty pieces of silver to the Ishmaelites, who took Joseph to Egypt.
and had him thrown into prison, where the king’s prisoners were confined. So Joseph was there in prison.
But the LORD was with Joseph and extended kindness to him. He granted him favor with the prison warden.
But Joseph said to them, “Don’t be afraid. Am I in the place of God?
You planned evil against me; God planned it for good to bring about the present result—the survival of many people.

stories.title: Thomas: the doubter
stories.note: Doubt met with presence, not rejection.

verses.text: But Thomas (called “Twin”), one of the Twelve, was not with them when Jesus came.

So the other disciples were telling him, “We’ve seen the Lord!” But he said to them, “If I don’t see the mark of the nails in his hands, put my finger into the mark of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will never believe.”
A week later his disciples were indoors again, and Thomas was with them. Even though the doors were locked, Jesus came and stood among them and said, “Peace be with you.”
Then he said to Thomas, “Put your finger here and look at my hands. Reach out your hand and put it into my side. Don’t be faithless, but believe.”
Thomas responded to him, “My Lord and my God!”
Jesus said, “Because you have seen me, you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen and yet believe.”

stories.title: John Mark: the quitter who came back
stories.note: He deserted; years later Paul calls him useful.

verses.text: Barnabas wanted to take along John who was called Mark.
But Paul insisted that they should not take along this man who had deserted them in Pamphylia and had not gone on with them to the work.
They had such a sharp disagreement that they parted company, and Barnabas took Mark with him and sailed off to Cyprus.
Only Luke is with me. Bring Mark with you, for he is useful to me in the ministry.

stories.title: The prodigal son (a parable, not a historical man)
stories.note: Jesus's parable; say 'Jesus told a story about...' not 'a man in history'. Nested quote marks in the source; keep them as printed when quoting.

verses.text: When he came to his senses, he said, ‘How many of my father’s hired workers have more than enough food, and here I am dying of hunger!
I’ll get up, go to my father, and say to him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight.
I’m no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired workers.”’
So he got up and went to his father. But while the son was still a long way off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion. He ran, threw his arms around his neck, and kissed him.
The son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight. I’m no longer worthy to be called your son.’
“But the father told his servants, ‘Quick! Bring out the best robe and put it on him; put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.
Then bring the fattened calf and slaughter it, and let’s celebrate with a feast,
because this son of mine was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found!’ So they began to celebrate.
